title: Shark-like fish were swimming before the first trees grew
body: Scales from shark-like fish turn up in rocks about **450 million years** old, from the Late Ordovician. The first trees, such as Wattieza, didn’t appear until roughly 385 million years ago, and the earliest dinosaurs not until about 230 million years ago. The lineage outlived the dinosaurs, though the sharks we know today, with their modern body plan, only show up in the fossil record around 200 million years ago.

slides.heading: Oldest first
slides.explanation: Shark-like scales: about 450 million years ago. Trees: about 385. Dinosaurs: about 230. Modern sharks: about 200.

events.text: Dinosaurs die out; sharks carry on

left.label: Popular claim
left.text: Sharks have existed unchanged for 450 million years.

right.label: Fossil record
right.text: The lineage is that old. Today’s shark body plan is about 200 million years old, and species have kept changing.

slides.heading: Why so few fossils
slides.text: Shark skeletons are cartilage, which rarely fossilises. Most of what we know comes from teeth and from the tiny tooth-like scales that cover their skin, which is why the early chapters of the story are told in scales.
